fields.System.Title: CNT-3 — Variance handling
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Turn a difference between counted and expected into either a correction or an investigation —
never into a silent adjustment.

Scope

In. Variance calculation, recount thresholds, approval and posting, investigation notes.

Out. General adjustments — that is [INV-7](../INV/INV-7-adjustments.md). Counting posts
through its own controlled path.

Design notes

Compare against the snapshot, not the live balance. This one line is the difference between
counting that works and counting that produces noise. A count entered at 10:05 against a
balance that changed at 10:02 shows a variance that is purely a timing artefact.

Never adjust before the recount. If the first variance is posted and the recount is then
compared against the adjusted figure, it matches perfectly — the problem vanishes from the
record while remaining in the warehouse.

The person who counted cannot approve their own large variance. Enforce in the service
layer.

CNT-304 is what makes counting improve anything. A variance corrected is a symptom
treated. A variance with an investigation note — "pallet found in the wrong aisle", "case
quantity wrong in master data" — aggregated over a month, is a list of things to fix.

Idempotency on posting. An adjustment posted twice on a retry corrupts the balance by twice
the original error in the opposite direction, which is deeply confusing to unpick.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Variance calculated against the live balance | [doc 09 §6.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Recount compared to the adjusted figure | [doc 09 §6.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Adjustment posted twice on retry | [doc 09 §3.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| High variance accepted without investigation | [doc 05 WF 10](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
